title: Tamsin and the Wreck
premise: Ulyana Crane, a railroad engineer who measures life in miles rather than years, is surveying closed lines along a monsoon-swollen river when the floodwater surrenders a chest stamped with the seal of Vessar, a nation that no longer exists. Inside are ledgers proving that a wartime atrocity was covered up by the very families who now govern the region — and Ulyana's own grandfather's name is in them, not as victim but as accomplice. Hunted by an heir who wants the chest destroyed and haunted by what inheritance truly means, Ulyana teams up with Tamsin, a river pilot with her own stolen history, to carry the evidence downstream through the storm. They survive the monsoon, outlast their pursuers, and choose to give the chest not to courts or governments but to the descendants of the drowned, ending the novel with Ulyana burning her grandfather's map and finally counting life in years.
about_author: Noor Oyelaran is a former hydrographic surveyor who spent six years mapping rivers across three continents before turning to fiction. Their stories explore how landscapes keep secrets and how ordinary people decide what justice owes the dead.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Establishes Ulyana's ritualized, distance-obsessed life surveying decommissioned rail lines after five years of self-imposed exile following a family estrangement. A letter from a lawyer about the grandfather's estate goes unopened. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness, the comfort of measurable things.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. During pre-monsoon flooding, Ulyana spots a shape snagged on a piling and retrieves a waterlogged chest bearing the seal of Vessar, a dissolved nation. The lock is broken but the contents are wrapped in oilcloth. Emotional beat: unease curdling into fascination; the first crack in Ulyana's ordered world.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Inside: shipping manifests, a ledger of deported families, and a signed requisition order bearing her grandfather's signature. Ulyana recognizes the station names from her own maps of closed lines. Emotional beat: vertigo — the past she fled has been riding the rails beside her all along.

chapters.title: Tamsin
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Introduces Tamsin Adeyemi, a river pilot running cargo through the delta, whose grandmother was listed in ledgers like this one. She notices Ulyana asking dangerous questions in port bars. Emotional beat: wary recognition between two people carrying different halves of the same history.

chapters.title: The Man from the Consulate
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A courteous stranger named Ivo Renner offers to buy the chest 'for archival purposes,' revealing he knows exactly what Ulyana found. He leaves a card and a threat disguised as concern for her safety. Emotional beat: the hunt begins; the chest becomes a target.

chapters.title: Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana deciphers that the ledger's route matches a rail line officially never built — one her grandfather surveyed. She opens the lawyer's letter at last and learns she inherited his papers, including a missing page referenced in the ledger. Emotional beat: grief and anger braided together.

chapters.title: A Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Renner's men search Ulyana's survey camp; Ulyana escapes with the ledger and barges aboard Tamsin's boat mid-loading. The boat takes on water; the monsoon front is two days out. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forged under pressure, trust still provisional.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin agrees to run Ulyana downriver but names her price: the ledger page listing her grandmother's family, whatever it says. They argue about whether truth heals or only wounds. Emotional beat: negotiation as intimacy; two definitions of justice collide.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Radio warnings confirm the storm will close the lower river for weeks — they must pass the checkpoint at Kessel Locks before it hits or be trapped. Renner broadcasts a false warrant naming Ulyana a thief. Emotional beat: the clock starts ticking audibly.

chapters.title: Kessel Locks
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A tense checkpoint passage where Tamsin bluffs past an inspector while Ulyana hides the chest inside a consignment of rail spikes. Renner waits on the far bank and watches them through binoculars, choosing patience. Emotional beat: narrow escape laced with dread.

chapters.title: The Drowned Station
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They shelter in a half-submerged rail station Ulyana knows from her maps. Among the rot she finds carved initials and dates matching the deportation trains. She tells Tamsin the full story of her grandfather for the first time. Emotional beat: confession as release; the walls come down.

chapters.title: Renner's Offer
chapters.summary: Renner's POV (first use). Reveals he is the grandson of Vessar's last interior minister, protecting his family's name and fortune. He reflects on why he cannot let the chest surface, and orders the locks upstream sabotaged to trap the boat. Emotional beat: chilling civility; evil as estate management.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The monsoon arrives early. They run the flooded gorge with the pump failing and the chest threatening to capsize them. Tamsin nearly goes overboard saving it; Ulyana pulls her back. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into loyalty — they are crew now, not strangers.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Drying the ledger by the stove, they find the missing page hidden in the binding: it proves Ulyana's grandfather later smuggled survivors out on the same closed line, then buried the evidence to protect them. Emotional beat: moral whiplash — inheritance is neither guilt nor absolution but both.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Fork
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Renner's hired boat corners them at the river fork. Tamsin uses her encyclopedic knowledge of seasonal channels to escape through a passage marked impassable, wrecking the pursuer instead. Emotional beat: triumph, but the boat is badly holed and the radio dead.

chapters.title: Beached
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Stranded on a shoal with a sinking hull, they argue about burning the chest to end the danger. Ulyana refuses; Tamsin admits she once sold information to survive and fears what she'd do again. Emotional beat: lowest point — trust cracked open and honestly examined.

chapters.title: The Village of Descendants
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Fishermen salvage them and bring them to a river village founded by deportees' descendants who have kept oral memory of the lost trains for three generations. The elders read the ledger aloud, matching names to living families. Emotional beat: awe — memory as a communal act of survival.

chapters.title: What Justice Owes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The villagers debate: courts, press, or quiet return? Renner arrives with mercenaries under cover of the storm's tail, offering money for the chest. Ulyana realizes giving it to any institution means it disappears again. Emotional beat: the theme crystallizes — justice outside the law must be delivered by hand.

chapters.title: Night of the Rising Water
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. Renner's men raid the village during peak flood. Tamsin moves the chest by canoe through submerged streets while Ulyana leads Renner onto a collapsing pier; the river itself nearly claims him before Ulyana hauls him out — refusing to become him. Emotional beat: action climax fused with moral climax.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In the village hall, the chest is opened publicly and every name read aloud over two days, copies made and distributed family by family so no single authority can bury it again. Renner, exposed before witnesses, retreats rather than massacre his family's shame into legend. Emotional beat: catharsis; justice as witness, not verdict.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin receives the page with her grandmother's name and learns she survived because someone on that closed line looked away. She and Ulyana part at the delta with promises and an open door. Emotional beat: bittersweet tenderness; what we inherit can be chosen.

chapters.title: Years
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV epilogue, one year later. Ulyana burns the grandfather's map of closed lines, keeps only the page of rescues, and takes a job building a new line — open, documented, accountable. The final image: measuring time in years at last, with a letter from Tamsin in hand. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; the mile counter finally stops.
